stance.summary: Dale highlights a persistent 'risk-off inflation market regime' driven by investor fatigue in tech megacaps following Meta and Tesla earnings, drawing parallels to the asset price declines of Q4 2018, while noting high short positioning raises short squeeze risk on rebounds.
stance.invalidation: An Nvidia or equivalent company demonstrating balance sheet discipline alongside booming earnings and expanding margins to truncate negative sentiment.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: The Meta and Tesla results and guidance supported the durability and severity of the current risk-off inflation market regime.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: Specifically, signals from Meta, CapEx up, stock down, and Tesla, CapEx down, stock down, point to investor fatigue with respect to most tech stocks amid historic concentration in the sector in the US and global stock markets.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: It will likely take an Nvidia or roughly equivalent company to demonstrate balance sheet discipline amid booming earnings and expanding margins to truncate the negative sentiment.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: Investors must respect the coincident and prospective implications of this spread widening for the global liquidity cycle.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: Per Goldman Sachs, hedge fund short positioning is near a 5-year high, raising squeeze risk on any rebound.

quotes.speaker: Darius Dale
quotes.text: If Q4 2026 winds up resembling Q4 2018 in risk-off inflation market regime terms, then these data suggest Q1 2027 is highly likely to resemble Q1 2019, which caused severe type II errors among the permabear community...

videos.gemini_evidence: Mark Newton appears via video link from Fundstrat and discusses market technical breadth, S&P 500 performance, and his positive outlook on market structure.

stance.summary: Mark Newton is bullish on US equities, noting that underlying technical market breadth is expanding with the equal-weighted S&P rebounding and market resilience persisting despite high bond yields and geopolitics. While expecting choppy conditions until past the midterms, he is very encouraged by the technical structure.
stance.timeframe: Near to medium term (until past the midterms)

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: Well, look, Scott, you've seen the equal-weighted S&P just in the last month rise to the highest level since early September. It's been a great comeback in the broader market at a time when technology yet again has been whipsawed and has started to pull back.

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: You know, the percentage of stocks above their 20-day moving average has actually doubled in the last two and a half weeks. So we've gone from 20% to about 45%. That is very encouraging at a time when we still have very elevated bond yields, crude is higher than what we want to see, and/or inflation, and obviously two ongoing wars.

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: My thinking is the market has started to stabilize, and so now we see a little bit of backing and filling in tech.

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: The broader market right now is is still doing very well. The S&P is less than 100 points from its all-time highs. We made new all-time highs just what, 11 trading days ago? So markets remain resilient, and earnings have started to kick off in very good shape thus far.

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: Well, look, you know, as as a technical analyst, we're taught really to ignore a lot of the exogenous events and the news. We know that headlines like that can affect stocks in the near term, headlines, but you know, we've seen the war ongoing most of the year, the S&P is up 13 and a half percent. It really pays to ignore what's happening as much as we want to concentrate on it, and really concentrate on earnings, concentrate on really technical strength and really what's driving this move.

quotes.speaker: Mark Newton
quotes.text: So, yeah, I'm encouraged. I think it's going to be a choppy time until we get past the midterms. I think we need to see evidence of bond yields, crude starting to peak and fall. That likely is still a little bit premature, but I'm very encouraged just with the technical structure itself with the market right now.
